source.reason: Hot-rolled hardness of 9Al-10Mn-1C is tabulated as 273 HV in Table 2 (b0019), repeated in Table 5 (b0051), Table 8 (b0083) and Table 9 (b0096).

The only quantitative property reported for the 9Al-10Mn-1C alloy in its hot-rolled (as-received) state is Vickers macro-hardness, 273 HV, appearing consistently in Tables 2, 5, 8 and 9 as the reference value used for all tempering comparisons.

unmapped_findings: The 9Al-10Mn-1C composition lies within the tested composition ranges of Table 1: Al 9–12 wt%, Mn 10–20–30 wt%, C 0.4–1 wt%, Fe balance.

No micrograph or morphological description of the as-hot-rolled 9Al-10Mn-1C condition is given in the paper; all reported microstructures (discontinuous precipitation at 600 °C, precipitation transformation, cellular transformation and spinodal decomposition at 800 °C) belong to the 600 °C/800 °C tempered samples and must not be attributed to this hot-rolled sample.

The hot-rolled 9Al-10Mn-1C hardness of 273 HV serves as the as-received reference/baseline in the tempering comparisons of Tables 2 (600 °C, 439 HV), 5 and 8 (800 °C, 356 HV) and Table 9 (600 °C, inter-lamellar spacing 'Narrow').

Minitab18® software was used to verify the consistency of the acquired hardness data (outliers excluded) and to plot data highlighting chemical composition and process effects; this data-analysis step is not specific to the hot-rolled condition.
